facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October. He is running on fumes due to his work.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October.

facts.heading: Work situation caused burnout
facts.content: Daniel lost a big client, and half of his team moved onto a rescue plan. He ended up doing three people's jobs.
facts.evidence: We lost a big client, half of our team group moved onto the rescue plan, so I ended up doing three people's jobs.

facts.heading: Work habits persist late
facts.content: Daniel is still answering work messages at 10 at night. He thinks about work even when not working.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by seven and I'm still answering messages at 10 at night. Even when I'm not working, I'm thinking about work.

facts.heading: Poor sleep quality reported
facts.content: Daniel reports terrible sleep quality. He sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about 4 hours.

facts.heading: Sleep waking time
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at 3 in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: I wake up at 3 in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Sleep routine involves work
facts.content: When Daniel wakes up, he has to start shipping schedules and check clients. He then calculates how little sleep he will get.
facts.evidence: We have to start shipping schedules, the clients, whether I've forgotten something. Then I look at the clock and I do the math on how little sleep I'm gonna get, which makes it worse.

facts.heading: Dreading the nights
facts.content: Daniel has started dreading the nights. He lies down for two to five minutes and gets up to make tea.
facts.evidence: Then I lie on two about five and get up and make tea. I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: my father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's current condition
facts.content: Daniel's father still himself, mostly. His hands shake, he is slower, and he gets frustrated.
facts.evidence: Still himself, mostly. His hands shake, he's slower, he gets frustrated.

facts.heading: Father is the strong one
facts.content: Daniel's father is having a dream and has always been the strong one.
facts.evidence: He's having a dream and he's always been the strong one.

facts.heading: Daniel drives father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel is the one who drives his father to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks, taking about an hour each way.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks, it's about an hour each way.

facts.heading: Sister lives in Toronto
facts.content: Daniel's sister Hannah lives in Toronto. All the care for their father falls on Daniel.
facts.evidence: My hungry sister Hannah lives in Toronto, so all the care for our father falls on me.

facts.heading: Daniel feels guilty about care
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for saying he is the one who is hearing about his father's care. He feels selfish being tired when his father is ill.
facts.evidence: Guilty for even saying it. It feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill.

facts.heading: Daniel avoids sharing feelings
facts.content: Daniel does not say anything to anyone about his feelings. He does not say anything to Hannah either.
facts.evidence: So I don't say anything to anyone. Not to Hanach either?

facts.heading: Daniel reports being fine
facts.content: Daniel tells Hannah he is fine when she asks how he is.
facts.evidence: She asks how I am, and I say fine.

facts.heading: Daniel's location at hospital
facts.content: Daniel stated that he sits in a car park at the hospital for 10 minutes before going in for appointments.
facts.evidence: That would be the point. She can't do anything from Canada. That I'm not fine? That some days I sit in a car park at the hospital for 10 minutes before I go in?

facts.heading: GP tests normal
facts.content: Daniel had blood tests, and they were all normal. The GP said it is stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She had blood tests. They were all normal. She said it's stress and exhaustion.

facts.heading: Claire is patient
facts.content: Claire is very patient and does not push Daniel to talk. Daniel sees that Claire is also hurting.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tan and doesn't push me to talk. But I can see she's wearing that hurt, too.

facts.heading: Claire stopped asking about weekend
facts.content: Claire stopped asking if Daniel wanted to go away for the weekend because he always said no. Daniel feels this is the worst part.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no. That's the thing I feel worst about, actually.

facts.heading: Emails cause anxiety
facts.content: Daniel feels that emails are what stops him from saying yes to plans. He has to respond to 200 emails if he is away.
facts.evidence: The emails. And if I'm away, I'll come back to 200 of them.

facts.heading: Rest has a price
facts.content: Daniel believes that even rest has a price. He cannot remember the last time he was properly off.
facts.evidence: So even rest has a price. Can't remember the last time I was properly off.

facts.heading: Stopped running two months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago. His legs feel like lead now. He has not gone back.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. My legs feel like lead. And I just never went back.

facts.heading: Lost a part of self
facts.content: Daniel thinks he has lost a part of himself. He felt running was the one time in the week nobody could reach him.
facts.evidence: I think I've lost a part of myself. It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Peterson sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast. Daniel answers them even when in bed.
facts.evidence: He sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast. I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed.

facts.heading: Fear of not answering
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that his boss will think he is not committed if he does not answer. He fears they might let him go due to restructuring.
facts.evidence: What are you afraid would happen if you didn't answer? Then he'd think I wasn't committed. There's a restructuring this spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Relief and guilt about job
facts.content: Daniel thinks he might feel relieved if he is let go. He also thinks he would feel horrible about being relieved.
facts.evidence: I think part of me would be relieved. I'd feel horrible about being relieved.

facts.heading: Irritable and moves apart
facts.content: Daniel is irritable and moves apart from the third person. He slept in a colleague last week or in nothing.
facts.evidence: A lot, mostly. And irritable. I slept in a colleague last week, or in nothing, and went and sat in the toilet for ten minutes.

facts.heading: Hearing shaking in head
facts.content: Daniel heard something going in his head that was shaking. He thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.
facts.evidence: I heard it was going in my head and it was shaking. We thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.

facts.heading: Previous frightening experience
facts.content: Daniel has experienced frightening episodes on a train to Manchester. He has not told anyone about this experience.
facts.evidence: Once on a train to Manchester, just to get off and stand on a platform. I haven't told anyone about it, not even Claire.

facts.heading: Coffee consumption habits
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day. He has started having one in the evenings to switch his head off.
facts.evidence: I want about 6 cups a day, and I've started having one in the evenings to switch my head off.

facts.heading: Alcohol consumption frequency
facts.content: Daniel drinks two glasses or sometimes three glasses of wine. He reports that the wine works for an hour.
facts.evidence: Two glasses, sometimes three. It works for an hour.

facts.heading: Feeling about wine use
facts.content: Daniel feels easy about the wine. He notes that it works for an hour.
facts.evidence: Easy. It works for an hour.

facts.heading: Waking time
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning.
facts.evidence: I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Feeling about coping
facts.content: Daniel believes he could cope with the rest if he could sleep.
facts.evidence: If I could sleep, I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Grandfather's behavior
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather worked at the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked at the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything.

facts.heading: Belief about being weak
facts.content: Daniel thinks his grandfather would think he was weak for being here. Daniel thinks he is not weak.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here. That I'm not weak.

facts.heading: Desire to change routine
facts.content: Daniel is willing to try a small change to fix time in the evening when he switches off his phone.
facts.evidence: Would you be willing to try something small? Fix time in the evening when you switch off your phone.

facts.heading: Proposed time for change
facts.content: Daniel suggested trying the change around half past nine.
facts.evidence: Yeah, half past nine, perhaps.

facts.heading: Current feeling state
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter after the session. He feels shaky after discussing things.
facts.evidence: Tired, but lighter. It's normal to feel a bit shaky after saying all that.

facts.heading: Needed to hear validation
facts.content: Daniel stated he needed to hear something said out loud. He expressed gratitude for hearing it.
facts.evidence: I think I needed to hear that

facts.heading: Anticipates next week session
facts.content: Daniel asked about the time for the next session. He mentioned the trains are awful.
facts.evidence: Same time next week? Yeah, I'll be here. I'll pray to make it on time. The trains are awful.
